email.title: Email
email.description: The backend alert notifications and password-reset emails are sent through. Off by default; a control plane started with APP_SMTP_* env vars still works until this is saved.

smtp.label: SMTP
smtp.presetsLabel: Quick fill for a known provider
smtp.passwordSet: A password is already configured. Leave blank to keep it.

ses.label: AWS SES
ses.secretSet: A secret key is already configured. Leave blank to keep it.

resend.label: Resend
resend.apiKeySet: An API key is already configured. Leave blank to keep it.

test.title: Send a test email
test.description: Sends one real email through the saved backend above, the same path alert notifications and password resets use.

email.comingSoon: More notification options are coming here: custom email templates, send-rate limiting, and per-alert frequency controls.
email.channelsCta: Looking for Slack, Discord, or webhook notifications instead?

wizard.others: Using AWS SES or Resend instead?

orphans.title: Leftover resources
orphans.description: Containers, volumes and certificates that no app or database accounts for. They are removed automatically once they stay orphaned past the grace period. Database data volumes are never removed.
orphans.empty: Nothing left over. Every container and volume belongs to a live app or database.

reason.stale_generation: Older release of a live app

toast.dryRun_one: Dry run: {{count}} resource would be removed.
toast.dryRun_other: Dry run: {{count}} resources would be removed.

authEngine.title: Sign-in engine
authEngine.description: Sign-in, sessions, API tokens, two-factor and passkeys run on the auth library {{version}}.

iamTemplates.title: Add a policy from a template
iamTemplates.description: Pick a ready-made policy. You can attach it to a user or token now, or later from the policy list.
iamTemplates.attachIdRequired: Enter the ID to attach to, or choose Nothing yet.

aiControl.title: AI control
aiControl.description: Decide what agents and the built-in assistant may do on this instance. The server enforces this on every request, whatever the token allows.
aiControl.navDescription: Turn agent access off, read-only or on, and limit it to chosen environments.

off.label: Off
off.description: Every agent request is refused. Humans are not affected.

observe.label: Observe
observe.description: Agents can read apps, logs and metrics, but not secrets, and change nothing.

operate.label: Operate
operate.description: Agents can read, write and deploy in the environments below. They cannot use root, change secrets, backups or instance settings.

admin.label: Admin
admin.description: Agents can use any ability their token holds in the environments below. A person must still approve protected deploys.

aiControl.adminUnavailable: Admin mode needs the experimental feature ai-control to be enabled on the server.
aiControl.envKindsDescription: Applies to operate and admin. Apps with no environment count as custom.
aiControl.viewAudit: View agent activity in the audit log

revoke.title: Revoke every agent token?
revoke.description: Every token with an agent label stops working immediately. This cannot be undone. The built-in assistant keeps working.

aiControl.loadFailed: Could not load AI control settings.

tokens.emptyBody: Create a scoped, revocable credential for the CLI, CI, or an MCP integration.
tokens.name: Name

create.title: Create token
create.description: A scoped, revocable credential for the CLI, CI, or an MCP integration.
create.name: Name
create.agentTip: Label the token as issued to an AI agent, for example "Claude Code". The name is shown here and on every audit log entry the token makes, so you can tell agent changes from human ones.
create.rootExclusive: Root cannot be combined with other abilities
create.signInApproveHint: Lets this token show your sign-in codes and approve new browsers from the CLI. Root does not include it and a device login never grants it, so keep this token short-lived.

hostFirewall.title: Host firewall
hostFirewall.description: Turns this server's ufw firewall on or off. Turning it on first allows SSH, the control plane ports and HTTP/3, so you cannot lock yourself out.
hostFirewall.confirmOnBody: These commands will run on this server, in order. SSH is allowed before the firewall is switched on.
hostFirewall.confirmOffBody: All ports on this server will be reachable again. This runs:
hostFirewall.missingHelp: Install ufw on this server to manage its firewall from here, or use your cloud provider's firewall.
hostFirewall.sshNote: SSH is on a different port? Set APP_FIREWALL_SSH_PORTS on the control plane before turning this on.
